cells.title: Keep a worktree for its capture queue only when it holds a note main lacks
cells.action: Red first, per contract ad9d30dc. In worktree/tests.rs, beside `fn a_non_empty_capture_queue_keeps_even_though_the_tree_reads_clean() {`, add a test where the worktree queue holds the same stub and flush lines as the main checkout's `.bee/capture-queue.jsonl` (write both files in the fixture) and assert the verdict is dead; run it and watch it fail for the reported reason (kept for capture-queue.jsonl non-empty). Then change the queue half of `fn precious_state_present(worktree_root: &Path) -> Option<String> {` in prune.rs (pass the main root from the call `if let Some(reason) = precious_state_present(&worktree_root) {` in classify_worktree, which holds `check.main_root`): write a strict local reader in prune.rs (do not reuse the capture.rs or nudges readers: they skip bad lines, which breaks D2). Split on newlines, strip a trailing carriage return, and skip blank lines. In the worktree queue, a line that does not parse as a JSON object, or whose `kind` is neither `stub` nor `flush`, or a `stub` or `flush` whose `id` is not a non-empty string, keeps. Collect pending stub ids: stub ids with no `flush` line of the same id anywhere in that file (order does not matter). In main's queue, collect every string `id` on any line (no pending fold): a missing file counts as empty; a file that exists but cannot be read, or holds a line that does not parse, keeps. Compare ids as exact strings, never trimmed or case-folded. Keep only when a pending worktree stub id is absent from main's set, with a message naming the count of such stubs, one example id, and the remedy `run bee capture list and bee capture flush --id <id> --into <doc> inside <worktree path>`. Leave the HANDOFF.json half unchanged. More tests: a unique pending stub keeps and names its id; a stub pending in the worktree but flushed in main reads dead; main naming the id only in a flush line reads dead; a worktree flush of main's pending stub reads dead; a worktree flush of its own unique stub reads dead; a flush line before its stub counts as flushed; a trailing newline and a CRLF file do not keep; an unparseable line keeps; a numeric id keeps; a missing main queue with a pending worktree stub keeps; the existing two capture-queue tests still pass unchanged. Update row 4 of the concept table and the doc comment above the check to say what now counts as precious, and that this repo tracks the queue while host repos ignore it. No new code comments.

A worktree whose queue holds a pending stub main never names is kept, and the reason names that stub
Every read or parse doubt keeps the worktree
